question: On 7 January 2025, US President-elect Donald Trump reasserted his vague hopes of annexing Greenland, while not ruling out the possibility of using military force. This announcement, hiding behind the trumped-up pretext of defending US national security, reveals expansionist, productivist and colonialist plans that are a serious threat to Greenlanders’ sovereignty and to the EU.

Greenland is a constituent country of the Kingdom of Denmark, which is an EU Member State. In addition, Greenlanders have repeatedly expressed their desire for autonomy, and the majority of the population now favours moving towards independence. Donald Trump’s provocations have already been strongly condemned by the prime ministers of Denmark and Greenland. 1.
Does the Commission plan to condemn this violation of the sovereignty of the Greenlandic people?
Will the Commission affirm its full support for the Greenlandic people and give them the necessary security guarantees?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (12.3.2025) The sovereignty of states must be respected. Greenland is an ‘Overseas Territory associated with the EU’, a partnership that showcases Greenland’s importance to the EU. Denmark and the United States (US) have been strong allies for decades and the EU is confident this will continue.

On the EU side, the EU will work towards a strong transatlantic agenda with the new US administration. EU-US cooperation and shared leadership is instrumental in addressing global challenges. Together, the EU and the US will address shared priorities for prosperity and international security, reaffirming the enduring strength of the transatlantic partnership.
